name: Carrier Identity Takeover
summary: Rather than inventing a company, the perpetrator adopts the identity of a real, licensed operator, typically one that is dormant, recently sold, or simply obscure. Every credential presented checks out because it belongs to a genuine business. Only the contact details, and the party actually collecting the freight, are substituted.
how_it_works: A real operator with valid authority is selected, often one that is inactive, recently dissolved, or has minimal online presence.
The perpetrator registers lookalike contact channels: a similar domain, a new telephone number, an email address that closely resembles the genuine one.
Genuine licence numbers, insurance references and registration data are presented, so verification against public registers succeeds.
Freight is awarded and collected under the borrowed identity.
The real operator is unaware until it is contacted about a load it never carried, or a claim it never caused.

indicators.signal: Contact domain is a close variant of the operator's genuine domain, differing by a character, a suffix or a top-level domain
indicators.observable_in: Onboarding contact record compared with the domain historically associated with the licence holder
indicators.notes: The strongest single indicator of this pattern, and cheap to check.

indicators.signal: Contact telephone or email details for a known licence number have changed recently and the change was not initiated through an existing relationship
indicators.observable_in: Change history on the carrier master record

indicators.signal: Bank details supplied do not match the account name of the licensed operator, or are held in a different country from the operator
Licence is valid but the operator has no recent activity, filings or movements
indicators.observable_in: Register filing history and any available activity data

indicators.signal: Equipment presenting at pickup is not registered to the licence holder
The genuine operator denies all knowledge of the movement when contacted on independently obtained details
indicators.observable_in: Direct verification using details from the register, not from the tender
indicators.notes: Always re-contact using details obtained independently. Contacting the number supplied by the perpetrator simply reaches the perpetrator.

false_positives.looks_like: Contact details for an existing carrier have changed.
false_positives.actually: Genuine rebranding, domain migration, office relocation, or acquisition.
false_positives.how_to_rule_out: Confirm the change through the pre-existing channel, not the new one, and require confirmation from a known contact. A genuine change survives verification through the old channel; a takeover does not.

false_positives.looks_like: Bank account name differs from the operator name.
false_positives.actually: Legitimate use of a factoring company or a group treasury account, which is common in road freight.
false_positives.how_to_rule_out: Require a written assignment or factoring agreement, and verify it with the factor directly. Legitimate factoring is documented and verifiable.

preventive: Treat any change to contact details or bank details on an existing carrier record as a high-risk event requiring out-of-band verification through the previously known channel.
Bind the carrier master record to a verified domain and telephone number, and alert on any deviation at tender.
Require that the payee name match the licensed operator, or that a verified factoring assignment be on file.
Verify licence status and licence-holder identity together, rather than checking only that a licence number is valid.
detective: Run automated lookalike-domain detection against the domains of onboarded carriers.
Flag tenders where a dormant licence suddenly becomes commercially active.
Reconcile equipment registration against licence holder at the gate.
responsive: Notify the impersonated operator, which is a victim and will usually cooperate, and which may already hold evidence.
Preserve the lookalike domain, email headers, telephone numbers and bank details, since these are the artefacts that link cases together.
Report to the licensing authority, because impersonation of a licence holder affects the integrity of the register itself.
Re-verify all counterparties onboarded in the same period through the same channel, since these campaigns rarely target a single shipper.

regulatory_hooks.relevance: A documented risk analysis of direct suppliers must identify this pattern class where the carrier population plausibly exposes the company to it.
Preventive measures listed here are the kind of control a company is expected to define and evidence once the risk is identified.
